updates.finding: Reuters reported ship-to-ship crude transfers in the Gulf of Oman had reached capacity limits as Saudi Arabia rerouted exports through Hormuz after disruption to its Red Sea route. Saudi crude exports via Hormuz were on track for about 3.6 million bpd in September versus about 900,000 bpd in August, increasing VLCC demand and freight costs.
updates.status: STS CAPACITY CONSTRAINT SUPPORTED; SAUDI HORMUZ RELIANCE MATERIALLY INCREASED; FREIGHT PRESSURE CONFIRMED
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE Hormuz workaround and Gulf of Oman STS logistics; preserve transfer-capacity/freight effects separately from Strait vessel counts.

updates.finding: Reuters/Kpler preliminary data put Thursday Strait of Hormuz commodity-vessel transits at nine, down from 14 the previous day and below a 10-day average of 18. Eight of the nine were exits; AIS-dark traffic remained an explicit undercount caveat.
updates.status: THURSDAY SEP24=9 TRACKED COMMODITY TRANSITS; BELOW RECENT AVERAGE; AIS CAVEAT RETAINED
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE existing Hormuz traffic series with Sep.24 preliminary count of nine while retaining prior daily figures and AIS caveat.

updates.finding: Reuters/Kpler reported 33.7 million barrels of crude had exited Hormuz so far in the week beginning Sep.20 on 19 tankers, broadly on pace with the previous week's 49.2 million barrels by the time of publication. The flow was dominated by Saudi crude followed by Iraq.
updates.status: SUBSTANTIAL CRUDE EXPORT FLOW CONTINUES DESPITE LOW VISIBLE VESSEL COUNT; WEEKLY DENOMINATOR PRESERVED SEPARATELY
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE shipping/energy context without treating crude-barrel and vessel-count denominators as interchangeable.

updates.finding: Reuters reported Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani military chiefs were to meet urgently under the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement to discuss support for Saudi Arabia amid Houthi attacks. Turkish parliamentary leadership separately said the pact still required Turkish parliamentary approval and was expected to be submitted after recess.
updates.status: URGENT MILITARY CONSULTATION CONFIRMED; TREATY IMPLEMENTATION STILL PROCEDURALLY INCOMPLETE IN TURKEY
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE Makkah pact from signed framework to active crisis consultation while preserving Turkish ratification status.

updates.finding: Turkey's parliament speaker said the Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey defence pact could eventually broaden into a wider Muslim-world framework that includes Iran. This was a political possibility statement, not an invitation accepted by Iran or a treaty amendment.
updates.status: EXPANSION POSSIBILITY PUBLICLY STATED; IRANIAN MEMBERSHIP OR NEGOTIATION NOT ESTABLISHED
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE regional-security architecture watch as a Turkish political signal only; do not treat Iran as a participant.

updates.finding: The U.S. ambassador to China said President Trump reiterated to Xi Jinping that direct or indirect Chinese help to Iran, including intelligence, parts or military equipment, was unacceptable. The ambassador said Washington received assurances from Beijing; Reuters did not independently establish the scope or implementation of any Chinese commitment.
updates.status: U.S. WARNING AND REPORTED CHINESE ASSURANCE ESTABLISHED; MATERIAL CHANGE IN CHINESE SUPPORT NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE China-Iran support/diplomacy watch; keep U.S. characterization and reported assurance separate from observed Chinese behavior.

updates.finding: Reuters reported Erbil and Sulaimaniya joined Baghdad and Najaf in suspending Iranian flights, meaning all four Iraqi airports then handling Iran service had halted those flights. This materially broadened observable implementation of U.S. aviation secondary-sanctions pressure.
updates.status: ALL FOUR ACTIVE IRAQI IRAN-SERVICE AIRPORTS SUSPENDED; IRAQ-WIDE IMPLEMENTATION FOR THOSE ROUTES ESTABLISHED
updates.drawer_effect: SUPERSEDE prior Iraq partial suspension status with all four operating Iran-service airports suspended; do not infer worldwide grounding.

updates.finding: The IDF publicly named Jabr Moqbel as a Hamas-linked money-exchange operator and Hasan al-Batta as a Hamas sniper killed in separate Sep.24 Gaza strikes. The identities and roles remained Israeli military attributions at this horizon and were not independently established by the sweep.
updates.status: TARGET IDENTITIES/ROLES ATTRIBUTED TO IDF; INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION NOT ESTABLISHED
updates.drawer_effect: UPDATE existing Gaza/Hamas strike drawer with named Israeli attributions while preserving source-bounded status.
